title: Aeternum by long duration — earth, hills, Canaan
source_text: II. Aeternum etiam quandoque dicitur id quod aliquando quidem finem habiturum est, sed tamen propter diuturnitatem, aeternitatem imitari videtur: sic quamvis caelum & terra olim transire debeant, tamen Ecclesiastae 1. dicitur terra in aeternum stare: & eodem sensu Deuteron. cap. 33. mentio fit a Mose, collium aeternorum, & eo quoque referri potest, quod decimo septimo capite Geneseos Deus pollicetur Abrahae se daturum illi & semini ejus, omnem terram Canaan in possessionem aeternam.
pass_a_gloss: Eternal is also sometimes said of that which will indeed sometime have an end, but nevertheless because of long duration seems to imitate eternity: so although heaven and earth must someday pass away, yet in Ecclesiastes 1 the earth is said to stand forever: and in the same sense in Deuteronomy chapter 33 Moses makes mention of everlasting hills, and thither also can be referred that in Genesis chapter seventeen God promises Abraham He will give him and his seed all the land of Canaan for an everlasting possession.
pass_b_english: Sometimes eternal = very long, still able to end.
Eccl 1: earth stands forever; Deut 33: everlasting hills.

lemmas.gloss: because of long duration seems to imitate eternity

choices.english: because of long duration seems to imitate eternity
choices.why: Second sense: long-lasting, not absolute eternity.
rejected: earth forever in Eccl 1 means the earth never ends
